properties.name: Congregational church
properties.basis: A frame church with a tower and spire at its south-east corner. Panorama No. 331 shows it from the west: a gable end with the spire standing behind the right-hand end of the roof, a little left of the Lodge Hall. That gives a sight line good to about 15 ft north-south. The Denver Public Library view from the east hill shows it close in the foreground; fitting that view's camera to five points on the Lodge Hall, the building north of it and a two-storey grocery puts the camera about 200 ft south of the July 1897 station, and the foot of the tower then falls on the No. 331 sight line, 215 to 285 ft from the camera. Measured on the close view the body is about 21 by 46 ft with an 8.7 ft tower. It stood at the east edge of block 33, fronting the avenue east of Collbran, beyond the edge of every insurance sheet. It fronted almost due east (bearing about 92, good to 3 degrees), 11 degrees off the street grid: both views from the east hill show about 75 px of its north wall, which a church square to the streets would hide. Good to about 15 ft north-south and 30 ft east-west. Built after 19 July 1897; in use by May 1898.

Its sight line, good to about 15 ft north-south, climbs the hill east of town and reaches a level crest about 130 ft above the flats exactly where the foot of the building appears in the photograph; beyond the crest the ground falls 50 ft in 100 ft to the bed of the lake, just north of the dam. viewer.evidence: The 1951 USGS Pikes Peak quadrangle draws a lake here, about 260 m by 75 m, in a side valley just east of town. Wolfe finished in January 1895, though no source says so outright. A dry meadow today. Outline scaled from the map, good to about 40 m.

properties.name: Dam of the lake (breached)
